title: Recursion tree where every node branches into two
summary: Each level down the recursion tree doubles the node count, so total workload sums across all levels.
context: Each square represents one operation, with the root counted as level 1. The top heading reads "Recursion tree — each node branches into two", and the right brace reads "A total of n levels" for a positive integer n.
description: The figure draws 1, 2, and 4 nodes on the first three levels, each non-leaf node branching to two children. Below level 3, 8 arrows lead into ellipses, and the bottom row draws 8 squares separated by ellipses purely schematically rather than fixing the bottom level at 8 nodes. The right column writes each level's count as a power of 2, while the decimal values in the table below are supplied by calculation. For n ≤ 3, only the levels that actually exist apply, and row n in the table coincides with the corresponding earlier row.

frames.title: Recursion tree where every node branches into two
frames.explanation: Summing all levels at the bottom gives 2⁰ + 2¹ + … + 2ⁿ⁻¹ = 2ⁿ - 1—that is, one less than 2 to the power n—giving O(2ⁿ). For the iterative cell-division code preceding the figure, level k represents the divisions performed in round k: n rounds perform 2ⁿ - 1 divisions in total to yield 2ⁿ final cells, which are not drawn as an extra row of operations. For exp_recur(n) following the figure, each square represents a call as the argument steps from n down to 1 across n levels, counting 1 per call and returning the same total.

tables.caption: Operations at each level of the recursion tree
rows: 2ⁿ⁻¹, that is, 2 raised to the exponent (n minus 1)
